name: upload_documents
title: Upload documents
description:
Upload local files once for parse_document, extract_fields and classify_document. A remote server cannot read local paths:
pass each file's filename, content_type and path, then run the returned document_request.command once, as returned.
It stores every file in DWS and prints an asset_id for each, in order. Pass an asset_id to the processing tool with the
same tenant_id, and reuse it for further operations on that file instead of uploading again. Uploading is free and processes
nothing; documents expire after 24 hours. The command's credential lasts at most five minutes: run it at once, and if it has
expired call upload_documents again.

documents.description: Local files to upload, 1 to 20: filename, content_type and path for each.

content_type.description: Document MIME type, such as application/pdf.

path.description: The file's path on your machine, exactly as your shell needs it. It only completes the returned command; the server never reads or stores it.

tenant_id.description: Optional tenant selector within the authorized product; DWS verifies ownership. Use the same one for upload_documents, the processing call and later reads.

status.description: awaiting_upload: run document_request.command now; it prints an asset_id for each file.

command.description: This request as a curl command with the credential and url filled in. Run it as returned once no <...> placeholder remains.

name: parse_document
title: Parse document
description:
Use it when the user asks to parse, OCR, transcribe or convert a document to Markdown, including a file attached to the chat:
DWS Parse returns OCR for scans, reading order, tables and element positions, as a stored run. For a question about a document
whose text you can read, read it yourself instead; parse a scan or an image-only PDF you can't read.
For a local file pass asset_id from upload_documents. Omit instructions for the default: agentic mode, visual reasoning with
self-correction, returning Markdown and spatial elements together in one pass; the second format costs nothing extra. Choose mode
text or structure only when the user wants a faster, cheaper parse. The call waits briefly and usually returns the finished run;
if status is queued or running, wait poll_after_seconds and use get_run until terminal. Then read what the task needs:
result.output.markdown for the text, or result.output.elements, JSON with each element's type, content and bounds.{x,y,width,height}
in rendered page pixels from the page's top-left; page gives width/height/pageIndex/pageNumber. Missing geometry is unknown, not zero.
When the result is compacted, read_result reads either with view=native and pointer /output/markdown or /output/elements, without
parsing again. Use extract_fields for structured fields.

instructions.description: Native DWS Parse configuration; omit for agentic mode with Markdown and spatial output. Choose inline mode/options/output or a stored processor with optional version/storeRun. Do not combine these modes.

mode.description: agentic: visual reasoning with self-correction for complex documents, the MCP default and the most costly; understand: semantic analysis; structure: OCR with geometry; text: plain text to Markdown, the fastest and cheapest.

processor.description: Stored parse processor ID (proc_…). Mutually exclusive with mode, options and output.

version.description: Published processor version: a positive integer, or the string 'latest' (the default). Only used with processor. Pin a numeric version for repeatable async submissions: omitted/latest may resolve to a newer version on retry and conflict with the original idempotency key.

options.description: OCR language detection options for structure, understand and agentic parsing.

language.description: OCR language: a string such as 'english', 'eng' or 'eng+spa', or an array of language strings such as ['eng','spa']. 'auto' enables automatic detection for Data Extraction.

maxLanguages.description: Maximum detected languages per page when language is auto. Default 2.

maxScripts.description: Maximum detected scripts per page when language is auto. Default 2.

output.description: Omitted: markdown and spatial together (markdown only in text mode). When output is supplied, choose exactly one of format or formats. text mode only supports markdown; other modes also support spatial. Multiple formats use one processing pass.

format.description: One output format; mutually exclusive with formats.

formats.description: One or more output formats. Mutually exclusive with format.

includeWords.description: Include word-level OCR inside spatial elements. Defaults to false.

useHtmlTables.description: Render Markdown tables as HTML to preserve merged cells. Defaults to true; requires markdown output.

enableSemanticBlockFormatting.description: Include semantic footnote, caption and picture markers in Markdown. Defaults to true.

includeHeadersAndFooters.description: Include running headers and footers in Markdown. Defaults to false.

extractWordsFromPictures.description: Include recognized picture text in Markdown. Defaults to false.

storeRun.description: Async Data Extraction always stores the native run using DWS quotas and retention. Omit or pass true; false is rejected before submission.

name: extract_fields
title: Extract fields
description:
Use it when the user asks to extract, pull out or get fields, values, line items or tables from a document, including a file
attached to the chat: DWS cites where each value comes from, as a stored run. Infer a concise intent from the user's request: MCP generates the schema with DWS
and extracts against it, so no parse call is needed first. intent and document_type are TOP-LEVEL arguments, never inside
instructions; omit instructions for this simple path. For a local file pass asset_id from upload_documents, for example
{"intent":"Extract the invoice number and total","asset_id":"3f2a9c1e-6b7d-4e8f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b"}. Alternatively supply instructions.schema or
instructions.processor. The call waits briefly and usually returns the finished run; if status is queued or running, wait
poll_after_seconds and use get_run until terminal. Finish the user's request with the values in result.output.data or
result_summary.data; use read_result for larger results and output_assets.download_request to save the native JSON.
metadata keeps per-field confidence and citations; schema is the generated schema, and schema_fields lists its top-level fields:
check they cover the request. For several files of one kind, extract the first, then pass the same intent with instructions.schema
set to its schema (result.output.schema, or read_result view=schema when the result is compacted) for the others: nothing is
regenerated and every file returns the same fields. generate_schema returns the
schema without extracting. Save MCP review warnings beside the native result, not inside it. Success does not verify accuracy:
report review signals (check before info), keep identifiers as strings and unanswered fields unknown.
For repeated tests or items, request individual records with their document/patient identifiers and dates.
If the user asks for a comparison, finish it after reading the records: match the same subject and test/item,
order by the relevant source date (collection date for labs, not report-release date), and compare only compatible units. Show the source values
and dates with the calculated change, labelled as derived analysis separate from native extraction data.
Do not silently match different subjects, missing dates, ambiguous duplicates or incompatible units; state those gaps. When you pass attached_file, read that file first and pass preview with the values you read: the Nutrient panel shows them right away, labelled as your reading, until Nutrient has the file.

intent.description: Top-level extraction goal inferred from the user: fields, grouping, formats and constraints. Never put intent inside instructions. Omit instructions for ordinary requests. For broad requests let DWS discover fields; do not invent unrequested fields. Exclusive with processor; with instructions.schema the schema is used instead of generating one.

instructions.description: With intent, optional schema/parseConfig/options/storeRun only. MCP defaults options.multimodal=true for visual layout, with higher cost/latency; explicit false is preserved. Without intent, supply schema or processor using native defaults.

processor.description: Stored extract processor ID (proc_…). Exclusive with intent, schema, instructions, parseConfig and options.

version.description: Published processor version: a positive integer, or the string 'latest' (the default). Only used with processor. Pin a numeric version for repeatable async submissions: omitted/latest may resolve to a newer version on retry and conflict with the original idempotency key.

schema.description: Explicit inline extraction schema; prefer the tool's intent to let DWS generate it. With intent, an earlier run's or generate_schema's schema replaces generation, normalized like a generated one, so files of one kind share their fields. Root type must be object. No $ref, $defs, composition or additionalProperties keywords. Limit 32 KB, 500 fields, 50 properties per object and 5 nesting levels.

name: classify_document
title: Classify document
description:
Use it when the user asks to classify documents or sort them into categories. Classify a document against at least two labels or
a stored classifier, as a stored DWS run. For a local file pass asset_id
from upload_documents. Preserve topK and text/image branch controls; no parse is needed first. The call waits briefly and usually
returns the finished run with native ranked predictions and scores; if status is queued or running, wait poll_after_seconds and
use get_run until terminal before reporting predictions.

name: generate_schema
title: Generate extraction schema
description:
Generate the schema extract_fields would use for an intent, without extracting: nothing is billed and no run is stored.
Use it to check the fields cover the user's request before paying for an extraction, or to fix one set of fields before
extracting several files of one kind. Pass the intent and document_type you would pass to extract_fields, and one input: asset_id
from upload_documents, document or source_run_id. Returns schema and schema_fields, its top-level fields. Then call extract_fields with the same intent and
instructions.schema set to this schema, edited if a requested field is missing.

name: sign_document
title: Sign PDF
description:

name: process_document
title: Process documents
description:
Process documents with native DWS Build instructions: conversion, merging and multi-step operations. Bind file/HTML
aliases through documents, each with filename, content_type and path; append a blank page with {page:'new'}. Generate a
fresh UUID yourself as idempotency_key for each new job. Run the returned document_request.command: it submits durable
Build and returns HTTP 202 job metadata. Save the complete job_handle (a job ID alone cannot recover it), wait
poll_after_seconds and call get_processor_job until terminal, then download the file to finish the task. After an
uncertain submission keep the same instructions, files, tenant and key; never invent a new key or retry automatically.
Some Build shapes are unsupported asynchronously. For PDF-to-Markdown prefer parse_document.

For an uncertain submission preserve this same key, exact instructions/files and tenant. DWS replays its original job while metadata is retained, including an expired result; this does not guarantee exactly-once worker execution.

name: read_result
title: Read run result
description:
Read selected values from an existing completed JSON result without downloading it through a
shell. It checks run status itself: no preparatory get_run is needed. No processing or upload
occurs. If queued/running, wait at least poll_after_seconds and use get_run for further status polls;
continue until terminal rather than answering with a queued acknowledgement. Start with view=data for extraction, review for warnings,
schema for field definitions, metadata for citations, or native for other product JSON.
Follow result_access directly when available; result_directory lists actual views, child paths,
array counts and string character counts. For parsed Markdown use native /output/markdown;
use total_characters to choose a suffix offset without reading the beginning first.
pointer is a JSON pointer within that view; empty selects its root. Array elements and object
properties are paged using offset/limit, with a byte budget that may return fewer items.
Follow result_view.next_offset; entries give child pointers when a whole item cannot fit.
To inspect data and supporting evidence together, prefer selections with up to four views
(for example data, metadata and review) in one call and one download. Omit the top-level
selection arguments when using selections. Each result_views entry reports its own outcome;
missing paths do not discard other selections. The global review_summary remains authoritative
about available warnings and source truncation; a selected subset cannot establish accuracy.
String values support text_offset/text_limit and return text_range. Follow its next_offset
to read long text without shell downloads; offsets count Unicode code points, not bytes.
Each selection returns at most 8 KiB of values, at most 32 KiB across four selections.
Never interpret omitted values as empty data. Full original evidence stays in DWS: download
the native result using output_assets.download_request when saving results; save MCP review separately. This tool does not write files.

omitted_signals.description: Canonical signals left out of this compact summary only. They remain readable with read_result view=review; this is not the count of warnings missing upstream.

source_truncated.description: The bounded MCP review is not exhaustive. Any additional missing warnings are unknown; this is independent of omitted_signals, which remain accessible.

output_assets.description: Existing DWS artifacts with authenticated download requests.

download_url.description: Native DWS asset URL; requires DWS OAuth. Use download_request for a harness without that credential.

command.description: This request as a curl command with the credential and url filled in. Run it as returned once no <...> placeholder remains.

result_access.description: Suggested read_result arguments for inspecting retained JSON without new processing or shell scripts.

result_directory.description: Available views and bounded paths/counts. Use string character counts to jump to a suffix; arrays are not expanded into records.

truncated.description: Some child paths were omitted by the depth/count/byte bounds; read a parent to explore further.

name: get_account_usage
title: Get account usage
description: Read account usage and credits for an authorized product. A balance is not a reservation, price quote or permission to execute. Recent asynchronous deductions may not have settled; do not claim a workflow was free from an unchanged balance.

product.description: Product whose usage and credits to read; the account must have access to it.

outputSchema.description: The product's usage and credit balance, as DWS reports it for the account.

name: studio_run_link
title: Open run in DWS Studio
description:
For the Nutrient document panel only. Returns the private DWS Studio link to a Data Extraction run; it opens
for a signed-in member of the run's organization, in the organization's default Data Extraction workspace.

tenant_id.description: Optional tenant selector within the authorized product; DWS verifies ownership. Use the same one for upload_documents, the processing call and later reads.

url.description: Private DWS Studio link; it requires signing in to the run's organization.
